prompt.context: Our client is Utility Co., a US-based utility company that operates on the West Coast of the United States. Utility Co. has been profitable over the last several years, and has seen relatively stable/favorable business conditions during that time. However, 2 weeks ago, regulators began pressuring Utility Co. to reduce its costs in order to improve prices/rates for customers. Utility Co. operates in a highly-regulated energy market, and is required to justify the prices/rates it charges customers through an annual process that examines a provider's cost structure and attaches a 'reasonable return' on top of its cost structure in order to arrive at prices/rates. The CEO of Utility Co., Larry 'Chipper' Jones, has engaged our team to identify where and how Utility Co. can reduce its costs by $500M.
prompt.question: Where and how can Utility Co. reduce its costs by $500M?

clarifying_info.q: What services does Utility Co. provide?
clarifying_info.a: Utility Co. provides both gas and electric services, but both businesses operate the same.

clarifying_info.q: What parts of the utility value chain does Utility Co. operate?
clarifying_info.a: Utility Co. is a fully-integrated utility, performing all functions of the utility value chain: generation, transmission, and retail.

exhibits.title: FY18, West Coast Utility Industry Costs
exhibits.shows: Bar chart comparing revenues and cost breakdown (Fuel/Inputs, Maintenance & Construction, Depreciation) for Utility Co. and Competitors/Peers, with an Asset Age & Use Index for each.

exhibits.title: Maintenance & Construction Activity Log/Observations
exhibits.shows: Observed daily activity log showing average time per worker spent on each activity throughout the day, with a note that labor agreements mandate at least 60 minutes per day for lunch and breaks.

framework: Segment costs by utility activities: Generation, Transmission/Maintenance, and Retail
Generation: cost of fuel (renewables, gas/coal, nuclear) and asset efficiency/throughput
Transmission/Maintenance: cost of maintaining assets (power lines), construction of new assets, labor TPT/efficiency
Retail: call center costs and TPT/efficiency, billing/payment costs, overhead/SG&A, building/infrastructure, technology/systems
Benchmark client costs vs. competitors to identify where the cost gap lies
Identify root causes of cost gaps and quantify savings potential

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the absolute cost difference between Utility Co. and its competitors. What is driving the gap?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate absolute costs for each bucket. Client total costs = $20B (25B rev - $5B implied from 80% cost ratio is not the right approach — read percentages off $25B revenue for client vs $18B total cost for peers). Strong candidate identifies that maintenance & construction is the driver of the cost gap, not fuel or depreciation. Asset Age & Use Index being equal for both (2.0) means the gap is NOT explained by older or more heavily used assets.

math.setup: Apply cost breakdown percentages to revenues to get absolute dollar costs. Client revenue = $25B, Peer revenue = $25B. Client total cost = $20B (implied: 30%+50%+20% = 100% of costs; cost/revenue ratio can be derived). Use the table in guidance: Client costs = $20B, Peer costs = $18B.
steps: Client: Fuel = 30% x $20B = $6B; Maintenance & Construction = 50% x $20B = $10B; Depreciation = 20% x $20B = $4B
Peer: Fuel = 33% x $18B = ~$6B; Maintenance & Construction = 44% x $18B = ~$8B; Depreciation = 22% x $18B = ~$4B
Cost gap: Fuel = $6B - $6B = $0; Maintenance & Construction = $10B - $8B = $2B; Depreciation = $4B - $4B = $0
Total cost gap = $2B, entirely attributable to Maintenance & Construction
math.answer: Utility Co. has $2B more in costs than peers, all driven by Maintenance & Construction. Fuel and Depreciation are comparable. Asset age and use are identical (index 2.0), so higher M&C costs are not driven by asset condition.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, identify wasteful time activities and quantify the potential savings. (Interviewer provides cost rate = $50/hr, workers per job = 10, annual jobs = 500K, and assumes 1 job can be completed in 1 day.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify addressable wasteful time: waiting for tasks/instructions (30 min), wait for materials (30 min), excess lunch beyond mandate, and excess breaks. Mandatory minimum is 60 min (lunch + breaks per labor agreement). Total observed non-productive time = 30 (wait tasks) + 30 (wait materials) + 30 (break 1) + 60 (lunch) + 30 (break 2) = 180 min. Addressable opportunity = 180 min - 60 min mandatory = 120 min = 2 hours per worker per day.

math.setup: Addressable wasted time per worker per day = Total unproductive time - Mandatory breaks. Then scale by workers per job, annual jobs, and cost rate.
steps: Unproductive/non-wrench, non-driving, non-admin time: wait for tasks 30min + wait for materials 30min + break 30min + lunch 60min + break 30min = 180 min
Addressable opportunity per worker per day: 180 - 60 = 120 min = 2 hours
Hours saved per job = 2 hrs/worker x 10 workers = 20 hrs/job
Annual hours saved = 20 hrs/job x 500K jobs = 10M hours
math.answer: $500M in annual savings — exactly the target — by eliminating 2 hours of wasteful time per worker per day across 500K jobs.

brainstorming.prompt: What tactics could Utility Co. use to reduce wasteful time among maintenance and construction workers?

categories.name: Performance Management
ideas: Measure and incentivize workers and teams based on number of jobs completed per day
Gamify performance by posting team standings publicly
Offer bonuses or awards for top-performing teams

categories.name: Planning and Scheduling
ideas: Assign jobs the day before to eliminate morning wait time for tasks/instructions
Deliver materials to job site prior to start of job rather than on the day of work
Pre-stage equipment and materials at job sites

categories.name: Process Improvement
ideas: Streamline team meetings and admin to reduce non-wrench time
Use mobile/digital tools for real-time job assignment and status updates
Improve routing/dispatch to reduce unnecessary driving time

recommendation: Utility Co. can achieve the full $500M cost reduction target by improving labor efficiency among field maintenance and construction workers
The primary lever is eliminating 2 hours of wasteful time per worker per day (waiting for tasks, waiting for materials, excess breaks) across 500K annual jobs at a $50/hr cost rate
risks: Push-back and adoption challenges from workers resistant to new performance management practices
Increased manager workload from additional performance tracking, measurement, and materials coordination responsibilities
next_steps: Partner with HR and technology teams to design and build performance management capabilities (tracking, dashboards, incentive structures)
Work with HR and frontline managers to craft messaging and roll out new performance management policies and systems to the workforce
